lessons.title: Getting Started with Arduino
lessons.source: Arduino Tutorial 1: Getting Started for Absolute Beginners — toptechboy.com
lessons.objective: Set up the Arduino, understand the IDE, and blink the built-in LED on pin 13.
steps: Every sketch has two parts: setup() runs once, loop() runs forever.
Tell the Arduino pin 13 is an OUTPUT: pinMode(13, OUTPUT);
Turn the LED on with digitalWrite(13, HIGH); and off with LOW.
Use delay(500); to wait half a second between changes.
Watch the LED blink — you have written your first program.

lessons.title: How LEDs Work and How to Control One
lessons.source: Arduino Tutorial 2: How LEDs Work — toptechboy.com
lessons.objective: Understand LED polarity and current limiting, then control an external LED.
steps: An LED only conducts one direction: long leg is the anode (+), short leg the cathode (−).
An LED must NEVER be connected without a current-limiting resistor.
Use a 220Ω resistor in series to keep current under the 20mA maximum.
Wire pin 13 → resistor → LED anode, then LED cathode → GND.
Blink it with the same sketch from Lesson 1.

lessons.title: How Breadboards Work
lessons.source: Arduino Tutorial 3: How Breadboards Work — toptechboy.com
lessons.objective: Learn how breadboard rows and power rails are connected internally, and build a clean circuit.
steps: The two long rails on each side are power buses: red for 5V, blue for GND.
Each 5-hole row in the middle is connected internally; the center trench splits left from right.
Bring 5V and GND from the Arduino to the rails first.
Place components across rows — never short both legs into the same row.
Rebuild the Lesson 2 LED circuit neatly using the rails.

lessons.title: Understanding Arduino Variables
lessons.source: Arduino Tutorial 4: Understanding Arduino Variables — toptechboy.com
lessons.objective: Replace magic numbers with named variables to make sketches readable and adjustable.
steps: Declare a variable for the pin: int ledPin = 13;
Declare variables for timing: int onTime = 500; int offTime = 500;
Use the variables in pinMode, digitalWrite, and delay instead of raw numbers.
Change onTime and offTime and re-run — one edit changes the whole behavior.
Good names make code self-documenting.

lessons.title: Understanding Binary Numbers
lessons.source: Arduino Tutorial 5: Working with Binary Numbers — toptechboy.com
lessons.objective: Learn how computers count in binary, preparing for the LED binary counter.
steps: Computers store everything as bits: 0 or 1, off or on.
Each binary place value doubles: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16…
An LED is a perfect one-bit display: on = 1, off = 0.
Next lesson: build a multi-LED binary counter.
